doc: Checked registry for the golden/fixture artifacts of the test suite (S4b-main registry; pre-S10 slice E made it a CHECKED registry). Every record in `in_test`, `golden_midi` and `fixtures` carries: `kind` (the section-implied class: in_test / golden / fixture), `commit` (LEADING a commit sha that resolves in this repository; the prose after it gives the task context), `produced_by` (the producer, in ONE of two honest prefix-required forms - `gen: <command>` when an in-repo writer exists (the command must run a tool of the WRITER registry and the artifact must be bound to that writer's explicit artifact list); `capture: <source>@<commit> (no in-repo writer) - <pointer>` when the bytes were captured from a run (where the bytes came from, the commit they were captured at, and a pointer to the capture record: a file that must exist plus a quoted anchor that must appear verbatim in it)). A `gen:` command may only use a tool listed in the WRITER registry of tools/lint_golden_manifest.py, bound to the explicit artifacts it writes. `produced_by` is a string (it then applies to every file of the record) or, for a MIXED record, an object mapping file -> producer that covers exactly the record's file set) and `files` (repo-relative path -> sha256 of that file: the LF-CANONICAL sha256 for text artifacts, the raw sha256 for binary ones). tools/lint_golden_manifest.py checks all of it (schema, sha256, produced_by form, artifact coverage, test/case rot, golden_midi consistency) and is a blocking CI gate. DOMAIN SPLIT: the FROZEN S2-entry slot bitmap (tests/golden/slot_bitmap.txt + its companion tests/golden/manifest.json, canonical sha d66faabf) is a DIFFERENT domain owned by tools/update_goldens.py + tools/lint_golden_pin.py and is deliberately NOT registered here; tests/golden/s2entry_gate.json is one-shot gate evidence and tests/fixtures/README.md is documentation - all three exclusions carry their reasons in the lint script. `in_test` records that pin literals in the test source only carry an empty `files` map plus "relational": true.

in_test.test: b10 ORT sidecar product pin (tests/test_ort_logits.cpp, [ort_logits] 'ort logits reproduces the committed sidecar's pinned logits values')
in_test.pins: tests/golden/ort_logits_values.txt: the committed logits sidecar's REAL output for ONE fixed prefix (count head 1, then bar 0, subbeat 0, track 1, pitch 60, duration 4, vel_bin 4 - the legal 7-id head, the same one the C++ test feeds): the 256 logits values of the last-position row as IEEE-754 binary32 bit patterns + the sidecar's own sha256 70961f32a8debe023924c5a54290f5e3946b95776112c9c776d88ae2bed58823 + the digest of the values' bytes (sha256 over the 256 little-endian float32) + the argmax (the decision vector, id 0) — GOLDEN class (script-generated: the real output of the committed training/model.logits.onnx, captured by tools/capture_ort_logits_golden.py). D-B10.2: the pin covers the values AND the sidecar's sha256 — BOTH live in THIS artifact (the sidecar's sha256 is the golden's model_sha256, and the same C++ case hashes the committed training/model.logits.onnx and compares it, so a silently changed sidecar — a different export, a different graph surgery — reds the pin). The record's files map holds this ONE artifact (one record per artifact, one producer per record: the capture tool that wrote it); the sidecar binary is not a second artifact of this capture, so it carries no record here. BIT-EXACTNESS (measured, not assumed): the capture ran on onnxruntime 1.31.0 (the repo's training venv) and the C++ provider on the pinned prebuilt onnxruntime 1.22.0 (src/inference/CMakeLists.txt) - the two are NOT bit-exact (217 of the 256 values differ in the last bits, largest absolute gap 2.86e-06, largest distance 193 ULP, same under every session-option combination), so the C++ side pins the IDENTITY (the sidecar's sha256, exact) and the DECISION (the argmax, exact) and compares the VALUES within a DOCUMENTED tolerance (1e-04, ~35x the measured noise). The C++ reader is strict: an unknown key, a missing key, a malformed value or a wrong row count fails loud. The golden's own header note states the tolerance (1e-04) and the measured divergence, so a reader of the golden ALONE cannot mistake the values for bit-exact.
